actual_interface_occurrences.text: Let $R$ be a commutative ring with $1$, let $q\in R^{\times}$, let $d,n\ge0$ with $d\ge n$, and let $H=H_{R,q}(S_n)$ ([[def-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]). Write $S:=S(d,n)=\mathrm{End}_H(M)$ for the type-A q-Schur algebra with $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\Lambda(d,n)}M^{\mu}$ the direct sum of the permutation modules ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-direct-sum-of-a-family-of-modules]]) and let $\{\varphi_{ST}:\lambda\in\Lambda^{+}(d,n),\ S,T\in T_0(\lambda)\}$ be its cellular semistandard basis ([[def-murphy-elements-and-murphy-tableau-elements]] for the underlying Murphy elements and [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]] for the standard basis along which this basis is defined). Put $\omega:=(1^n,0^{d-n})\in\Lambda(d,n)$, the length-$d$ composition with $n$ entries equal to $1$ (legitimate because $d\ge n$), so that the Young subgroup $S_\omega$ is trivial and $m_\omega=1$; hence $$M^{\omega}=m_\omega H=H$$ is the regular right $H$-module. Let $t^{\omega}$ be the unique standard $\omega$-tableau, with entries $1,2,\dots,n$ down its single column; it is in particular the unique row-standard $\omega$-tableau whose entries increase down the column. Set $$e:=\varphi_{t^{\omega}t^{\omega}}\in S.$$

actual_interface_occurrences.text: Let $F$ be a field, $q\in F^\times$, $\ell=e(F,q)$, and $n\ge r\ge1$; at the empty lower-rank boundary put $S(0,0)=H(0)=F$ with its identity functor. Use the left-module version of the q-Schur algebra $S(n,r)$ and its exact Schur functor $f_{n,r}:V\mapsto eV$ with left adjoint $h_{n,r}:X\mapsto S(n,r)e\otimes_{eS(n,r)e}X$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]). Right-module suppliers are converted to left modules through their star anti-involutions. All Specht and simple labels below are **Murphy labels**: $f(W^\mu)=S_{\mathrm M}^\mu$ and $f(L_n(\mu))=D_{\mathrm M}^\mu$, the latter nonzero exactly when $\mu$ is $\ell$-restricted ([[thm-schur-functor-sends-weyl-and-simple-modules-to-specht-and-hecke-simple-modules]]).

[F1] The permutation-summand realization is $S(n,r)=\operatorname{End}_{H(r)}(\bigoplus_\alpha M^\alpha)$, with weight projections $1_\alpha$. The regular summand for a composition with exactly $r$ entries equal to $1$ is $M^\alpha=H(r)$. The standard corner is $\omega=(1^r,0^{n-r})$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]], [[def-schur-idempotent-and-schur-functor-for-type-a-q-schur-algebras]]).

[F4] Every Schur simple $L(\mu)$ is its nonzero cell-form quotient, so the descended symmetric associative form makes $L(\mu)^\circ\cong L(\mu)$ under Schur star. The normalized maps are $\varphi_{ST}(x_\nu h)=m_{ST}h$, with $m_{ST}\in x_\mu H\cap Hx_\nu$ and $m_{TS}=m_{ST}^*$; Schur star is $\varphi_{ST}^*=\varphi_{TS}$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). The standard coefficient trace satisfies $\tau(ab)=\tau(ba)$ and $\tau(T_u^*T_v)=\delta_{uv}q^{\ell(u)}$; its complete generator-block proof is the actual standalone trace construction of [[lem-dj-bridge-murphy-cellular-basis-and-cell-form]] and [[thm-standard-basis-of-the-generic-type-a-hecke-algebra]]. The following proof establishes the restricted-socle conclusion locally over the original field; no quantum-hyperalgebra square-root or unproved classical-specialization premise is used.

actual_interface_occurrences.text: Let $F$ be a field and $q\in F^{\times}$ with quantum characteristic $e$ ([[def-quantum-characteristic-of-an-invertible-hecke-parameter]], [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]]), let $n\ge0$ and $d\ge n$, and let $W^{\lambda}_F$ be the Weyl modules of $S_F(d,n)$ ([[def-type-a-q-schur-algebra-and-weyl-modules]]). Then for partitions $\lambda,\mu\vdash n$ with at most $d$ parts, $W^{\lambda}_F$ and $W^{\mu}_F$ lie in the same block of $S_F(d,n)$ if and only if $\lambda$ and $\mu$ have the same $e$-core ([[def-e-core-e-quotient-and-e-weight]]). Consequently, for finite $e$, the blocks of $S_F(d,n)$ are indexed by the $e$-cores $\gamma$ with $|\gamma|\le n$ and $|\gamma|\equiv n\pmod e$, and the block of $W^{\lambda}_F$ is determined by $C_e(\lambda)$. For $e=\infty$ we set $C_\infty(\lambda):=\lambda$; the algebra is semisimple and its blocks are indexed by the partitions of $n$.
